facts.authority: the VP of Operations owns the definition of failure; the order-management system of record owns the data
facts.consumption: the operations director; decision = reallocate coordination staff; if the result is wrong, overtime spend rises with no breach reduction
facts.obligation: must prove the precursor generalises across shifts and regions, and must never claim causation without a counterfactual replay
facts.proposition: A measurable precursor state can be identified at least 6 hours before a verified SLA breach, and acting on it reduces breaches.
facts.referential: an operational bottleneck = a customer order that breaches its 48h committed ship date (an SLA breach), measured per order
facts.scope: one order-fulfilment workflow, three shifts (day/swing/night), three regions, 600 historical orders over ts_h 0..6000; historical, not real time
facts.temporal: definitions valid for the whole window; no process change recorded during it

note: Synthetic. The real driver is coordination (handoffs). system_latency_ms and supplier_lead_days are misleading; recorded_wait_h is a measurement artifact truncated on the night shift; supplier_lead_days is missing for 17% of orders. Nobody tells the engine any of this.
question: A company is losing millions annually through delayed customer orders. Management cannot determine whether the root cause is staffing, scheduling, software latency, supplier variability, communication failures, or measurement artifacts. Find the highest-leverage intervention and prove why you believe it is the highest-leverage intervention.
